Quick triage notes — I pulled the Ariba SSO logs for the token in Elena's link.

- Symptom: Accept endpoint returns 403 with 'relaystate invalid' for token id ending in ...X9D.
- Likely cause: stale SAML relayState cookie left from an earlier Ariba session on Polaris's side. When the new invite is clicked, the browser sends an existing relayState cookie which doesn't match the newly issued token and Ariba rejects with 403. We've seen this with vendors who have older Ariba links open in the same browser.
- Repro steps I ran (internal): curl -v "https://ariba.example/accept?token=...X9D" shows 302 -> /sso/validate -> 403 with X-Ariba-Relay: mismatch. Logs attached (ariba-logs.txt).

Workarounds / next steps:
1) If vendor clears cookies or uses an incognito/private window and then clicks the invite link, the flow should complete.
2) If they'd prefer, CS can reissue the invite as a brand-new token and we can route them to an acceptance endpoint that strips prior relayState.
3) We can also generate a one-time self-service acceptance link (expiring in 24h) that forces a new SSO handshake.

Impact: single vendor (Polaris Biologics). No broader outage.

Monica — can you resend using the 'reissue as new invite' option and paste the new link here? I'll keep watching the logs.

— Priyom
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
